rated_messages.input_message: You were often stressed in this location and this might trigger urges. What can you do to reduce your stress here? If you can avoid this place until things settle down, then do.
A funny thing about people is that we tend to believe what we tell ourselves. So make sure that whatever else happens today, tell yourself "I can, and I will stick to not smoking!"
Some people find that having a simple mantra can really help, especially if things feel stressful. Try repeating something simple to yourself like: "I can do it!".
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking when you are here? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.

Imagine your urge is like a talk radio station going on about something you disagree with. Arguing with it doesn't change what they say. Instead, just let them talk while you focus on what's important to you.
Notice how stress and anxiety may pull you and make you want to smoke. Just notice this. You can choose to just notice and not smoke.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.

Did you know that just seeing other people smoke activates a part of your brain that is connected with the action of you smoking? This can bring on strong urges to smoke. One simple solution is to avoid seeing others smoke.
Have confidence in knowing that you can have this urge, choose not to smoke, be okay, and choose to do things that matter most to you.
